subject_entity.notes: North African council convened under Cyprian c. 251 after the Decian persecution to establish policy on the readmission of the lapsed; distinguished categories of lapse and mandated graded penance under episcopal authority; opposed both the rigorist position (Novatian) and the lax granting of peace by confessors.

object_entity.notes: Major North African city; center of Latin Christianity from Tertullian through Cyprian and Augustine; seat of important regional councils.

evidence.notes: De Lapsis reflects the council's policy on readmission of the lapsed at Carthage.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: But to those who have stood firm and have not been overthrown, what great joy! To those who have lapsed, medicine is not to be denied; but the lapsed must not assume that peace can be given them hastily by anyone. Let them knock at the door of the Church, but not with violence to break it down; let them beg but not presumptuously demand. Proper penance under the bishop's authority must precede reconciliation.
passage.notes: Graded penance under episcopal authority; against hasty reconciliation by confessors
